rationales.A: Closed, strike, and lock-out are all words for a shut mill during a labor fight.
rationales.B: The signs say closed and lock-out, not burned.
rationales.C: A lock-out means workers were kept out, not welcomed back.
rationales.D: The signs say closed and lock-out, not hiring.
rationales.general:
Read the signs on the mill.
1. One sign reads CLOSED—STRIKE and another reads LOCK-OUT.
2. A strike means workers stopped work; a lock-out means the company shut them out.
3. Both words describe a mill shut during a fight.
4. So the mill was closed while the company and the workers fought.
Remember: signs in a cartoon state the facts the artist wants you to see.

stimulus.text: Political cartoon “Promise and Performance,” published in 1892. A large Andrew Carnegie sits on piles of money bags, holding a whip. Below him stretches a steel mill with signs reading “CLOSED—STRIKE,” “CLOSED,” and “LOCK-OUT.” Crowds of workers stand outside the mill gates.
